speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; did the rash appear on your body before or after you started the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Morbilliform drug eruption (likely due to amoxicillin). The clinical presentation of an itchy, generalized rash appearing after antibiotic initiation for sinusitis is consistent with a benign exanthem; however, the specific mention of initial involvement of the antecubital and popliteal fossae with joint pain and fever raises concern for Acute Rheumatic Fever or Kawasaki disease. Given the timing and specific distribution, I need to distinguish between these possibilities. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential, Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), C-Reactive Protein (CRP), and Antistreptolysin O (ASO) titer. REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical photograph of the rash distribution.
